posts.body: I think you can just make an enemy file with the different frames, put on enemy initialize index and animationTime 0 and setframe method to index 0, then put on BattleManager update or whatever to add +1 to the animationTime for all alive and appeared enemies, if it's above a certain value add to the index. Then reset the timer and reset the index based on fixed value or enemy notetag. And make it use the setframe method based on the index, y can stay the same, x is like graphic width / number of frames * index (and width is graphic width / number of frames).

posts.author: Ludovinsky
posts.body:
My “breathing” idea is just a lightweight way to add slight, atmosphere. In my game it's gonna be used to just make rare capturable monsters stand out a bit more than the regular ones. What you’re describing though (mouths, galaxies, twitching limbs) is full expressive animation. Visustella can handle that, but it’s heavy and you’ll likely need to track down the plugin conflict that’s stopping you.
For subtle idle motion, a small plugin works fine. For enemies that
really
move, Visu is probably the only suite built for it. I mostly design my own plugins so I can avoid conflicts and tailor them to my game, like my time engine that flips a money hour/witching hour switch at 3:33am/pm and handles all my tinting through time switches. That way I never have to fight with plugin overlap.
